newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Moderate gain seen for Lee & Man debut.
newsitem.headline: Moderate gain seen for Lee & Man debut.

text.p: Shares of Lee & Man Holdings Ltd, a handbags and paper products maker, should show a moderate rise on the first day of trading on Wednesday based on continuing demand for new issues, analysts said on Monday.
Analysts said investors were attracted by prospects of making short term gains on the stock.

"A moderate gain is expected in view of its grey market price, but a strong rise in price is unlikely when investors find no reason to hold (the shares)," said a sales manager at a regional brokerage.
Analysts said the grey market price was HK$1.20 on Monday.
Lee & Man makes paper packaging products such as corrugated cardboard and boxes. It also manufactures and exports handbags and soft luggage, and audio cassettes.

Lee & Man offered 206.25 million shares at HK$1.00 each in an initial public offering (IPO), which concluded last week. Of the total, 185.625 million shares were offered to Hong Kong investors and 20.625 million shares reserved for employees. The public offering was 25 times subscribed.
The paper business accounted for about 28 percent of the company's turnover in 1996, handbags about 62 percent and audio cassette about 10 percent, the company said in its listing document.

Ricky Tam, senior research analyst at Delta Asia Securities, said the company was "not that exciting" in comparison to recent IPOs of red chip stocks. The popularity among investors of the Hong Kong listed, China-backed companies, has sent their prices soaring.

Henry Lui, research analyst from Mansion House, said the market was concentrated on Beijing Enterprises Holdings Ltd. The float of Beijing municipal government backed Beijing Enterprises in Hong Kong has created an unprecedent response from retail investors during its offering last week. Analysts said they expected investors would use profits from buying Lee & Man to invest in Beijing Enterprises when it debuts on Thursday. -- Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843 6370
